- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 80), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5–10% above recent peak or use mean reversion to 10-day moving average.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overreacts to sentiment shifts — if sentiment flips from positive to negative, delay forecast adjustment until 2–3 days later to avoid lag.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate mean price in early forecast window; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for first 7–10 days, then revert to trend.
- When sentiment is high and price is near 80+, model often forecasts higher than true outcome; use sentiment-weighted smoothing: reduce forecast by 0.3–0.7x sentiment value if sentiment > 0.7.
